results.summary_before: This project implements a 4-bit arithmetic logic unit with 13 selectable operations, including addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, bitwise logic, shifts, and modulo. The two 4-bit operands are provided on the eight input pins, while three bidirectional pins select the operation and the eight output pins present the 8-bit result. The design is intended for educational use and requires external digital logic such as buttons or sensors to provide inputs and observe outputs. The documentation is clear but contains a contradictory testing note about a counter, which appears to be a copy-paste error.

results.summary_before: This is a simple FP8 multiply-accumulate module implemented in Chisel, taking two 8-bit floating-point inputs and producing an 8-bit result after three clock cycles. It includes a partial register at address 0x00 as the starting value and is intended as a building block for systolic arrays and hardware accelerators. The design is self-contained and requires only an output buffer to store partial products and results. Testing is done by running make in the test directory, and the documentation is otherwise brief.

results.summary_before: This design is a configurable 8-bit ALU with registered inputs, eight arithmetic and logic operations, and eight configurable status flags. Inputs A and B arrive on the dedicated input pins, ALU control, register enable, and flag control come from the bidirectional pins, and the eight-bit result appears on the outputs with a status flag on a bidirectional pin. It requires synchronous operation with a toggling clock and an active-low reset pulse before use, and it is self-contained with no specialized external peripherals. The documentation describes the architecture as optimized for educational digital design and compact ASIC implementation, though the one-line description says 4-bit while the pins and title indicate 8-bit.

results.summary_before: This Verilog design outputs a waggling 6-bit rainbow demo on VGA, with effects controlled by input pins. Inputs enable dual mode (horizontal flip per scanline) and horizontal waves, with offsets controlling wave speeds. It requires a TinyVGA PMOD and runs at 25.175 MHz. The design can be tested in a VGA playground or with hardware, and an incomplete cocotb testbench is provided.
